chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Practising all the time and his strict father
summary: He blew the trumpet constantly, his father locked it away Sundays, took him to dances and made him be home before midnight.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, he seen that the only thing that I wanted was the trumpet and music, see. And that he didn't have to make me study or do anything. Sometimes on Sundays, he would have to take the trumpet from me.
Yeah.
And lock it up in the closet.
Why? How many hours a day would you blow?
I'd just blow it all the time.
Really?
Yeah.
(Laughter)
Really. Is that right. Well, I'll be darned.
So there was these kids, see, their parents would have to get after them to practice.
Yeah. To make them practice.
Yeah.
Yeah.
But not me. They'd have to stop me.
Well, I'll be darned. Well, did you -- what about -- did you have neighbors, pals, or guys that you ran around with on the street? Or --
No.
You just really had your mind on music, didn't you?
Yeah.
Honestly?
That's right.
You didn't go out with any girls or anything?

No. I'll tell you the reason why. My father, when I got big enough to go out and play dances with bands, my father would go with me. And as soon as the dance would be over, he'd bring me back home. I never did get a chance to go out with girls.
Well --
Until I left home, to go down to Florida.
Well, I'll be darned. Well, I think -- I mean, when you think that your father was a gambling man, it's amazing how strict he was, then, about everything.
Yeah. Very strict. Very strict on me.
I guess the thing was that he knew that life very well, and he decided that you weren't going to have that life.
That's right. And another thing he was strict on, you had to be in that house before 12:00 o'clock.
Is that right?
Yeah. All of us.
Fancy that. Well, that's remarkable, isn't it?
Yeah.
Yeah.
He wouldn't care if it was the oldest one, or any one of us, we had to be in that house before 12:00 o'clock at night.
